title: Emergency vaginal breech delivery
stem: ED delivery room. A woman at 38 weeks arrives fully dilated with the baby's buttocks visible at the introitus (extended breech). The obstetric team is 10 minutes away. Deliver the baby on the manikin.
notes:
Checked against RCOG Green-top Guideline 20b (Management of breech presentation, 2017) and ALSO.

Principle: 'hands off the breech'. Let the breech deliver spontaneously with maternal effort; do not pull. Only touch when needed: legs may need flexing out (Pinard) if the breech hangs; keep the fetal back anterior (sacrum anterior). Loop of cord: do not pull. When the scapulae are visible, deliver the arms: if they are not delivered spontaneously, Løvset's manoeuvre (rotate the body 180° holding the pelvis to bring each arm under the pubic arch). Let the body hang to encourage head flexion, then deliver the head with Mauriceau–Smellie–Veit (fingers on the malar bones to flex the head, other hand on the occiput) or forceps. Neonatal team present. Anticipate cord compression and head entrapment.

Your notes say footling and incomplete breech are 'unsafe for vaginal delivery'. That is true for planned delivery, but in the ED if birth is imminent the baby still has to be delivered vaginally while waiting for obstetrics; the same hands-off principles apply.

steps.hint: Hands off; back anterior; arms (Løvset); let it hang; Mauriceau–Smellie–Veit for the head.

opts.t: Let the breech and legs deliver with pushing; touch only to flex out a leg that is stuck
opts.mark: Allows spontaneous delivery of the breech

opts.t: Keep the baby's back anterior; wrap the body in a warm towel
Scapulae visible, arms not out: Løvset's manoeuvre (hold the pelvis, rotate 180° each way)
Let the body hang for a few seconds until the hairline shows
opts.mark: Lets the body hang to flex the head

opts.t: Mauriceau–Smellie–Veit: fingers on the cheekbones, other hand on the occiput; flex and deliver the head slowly
opts.r: The head delivers slowly. The baby cries.

opts.t: Pull on the legs to speed it up
opts.r: Traction causes arm extension and head entrapment.

opts.t: Hold the body up high above the mother's abdomen immediately
Baby to the neonatal team; active third stage with oxytocin 10 IU IM
Check hips later (breech is a risk factor for hip dysplasia)
